summary: Backend + frontend E2E for new secure auth workflow. Backend: 31/31 pytest cases pass covering login (admin/employee/invalid), /auth/me, /auth/change-password, /profile, role isolation (employee blocked from GET /employees, add employee, vendor create/update/delete, other-employee activity/collections/dashboard; admin blocked from POST collections/expenses), admin-only employee activity endpoint, dashboard, duplicate-phone rejection, employee scoping of dashboard/collections, identity spoofing prevention on POST /collections & /expenses, logout. Frontend: admin login->admin profile shows 'Administrator account'; logout returns to login; new employee created via admin API and can log in through the UI, sees forced ChangePasswordDialog, submits new password successfully, portal switches to Employee view (name/territory shown). Server-side 403 confirmed from the employee's browser session for /employees, /employees/emp-raj/activity, /collections?employee_id=emp-raj, /dashboard?employee_id=emp-raj, POST /vendors. Identity spoof attempt on POST /collections rejected: server overwrote employee_id/employee_name with the signed-in user. Mobile (390x844) login page has no horizontal overflow. Fixed one critical model-definition bug during testing.

critical.issue: Collection and Expense pydantic models did not declare employee_id/employee_name fields. Because pydantic v2 ignores extra kwargs by default, router.py's `Collection(**payload.model_dump(), employee_id=user['employee_id'], employee_name=user['name'], ...)` silently DROPPED the identity fields before insert. Result: every newly created collection/expense was persisted without an employee_id, making them invisible to employee-scoped queries and un-attributable in admin activity. This directly defeated requirement #6 ('employee identity is enforced server-side even when payload tries another identity'). FIXED by testing agent: added `employee_id: str` and `employee_name: str` to Collection and Expense models in /app/backend/models.py.

minor.issue: Seed is idempotent (only inserts users if not exists). If a testing agent changes the seeded employee's Welcome@123 password once, subsequent runs of the seeded-employee login test will 401. `test_seeded_employee_login_and_flag` handles this via pytest.skip, but a hard reset endpoint (or a flag) would make regression runs deterministic.

Legacy collections/expenses created before the model fix would fail response_model validation forever. Testing agent purged 1 collection + 1 expense that lacked employee_id/employee_name. Prod-safety: consider a one-shot migration/backfill if this app is fielded with existing data.

backend/.env sets CORS_ORIGINS=* while server.py uses allow_credentials=True. Browsers reject wildcard-with-credentials, so httpOnly cookie login is effectively non-functional cross-origin (the Bearer-token fallback saves the frontend). Set CORS_ORIGINS explicitly to REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL for prod.

action_items: Confirm/keep the models.py additions (employee_id, employee_name on Collection & Expense) — these are required for the security guarantee to hold.
Tighten CORS: replace '*' with the explicit frontend origin so httpOnly cookies work cross-origin.
(Optional) Add a data-migration step for pre-existing collections/expenses without employee_id, or make the fields Optional[str] with a placeholder to avoid response_validation 500s in the wild.
critical_code_review_comments: models.py: Collection & Expense were missing employee_id/employee_name fields — biggest issue, fixed.
auth.py: require_admin is a no-op (`Depends(lambda: None)`). Not currently used but leaving it there invites accidental use. Delete or wire to `current_user` with a role assertion.
auth_routes.py login: response.set_cookie uses secure=True — correct for prod, but ensure REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL is always https in dev/preview (it is here).

router.py update_employee resets password_hash and must_change_password=True on EVERY edit (name/territory changes) because payload.temporary_password is required. Splitting into a 'reset password' endpoint would avoid forcing password resets on trivial edits.

router.py: extra fields on CollectionCreate/ExpenseCreate are silently dropped by pydantic — combined with the model-drop bug this was catastrophic. Consider `model_config = ConfigDict(extra='forbid')` on the *Create schemas so spoof attempts get a 422 instead of being silently overridden.
seed.py is not idempotent for passwords — if seed employee password is rotated, seed doesn't re-establish Welcome@123. Playbook step #5 expects idempotency.

success_rate.frontend: 100% for the security flow (admin login/profile/logout, employee login+forced password change, all 5 admin routes 403 for employee, spoof rejected, mobile overflow OK)

test_credentials: Admin phone 9999999999 / Admin@123 (unchanged). Seeded employees still on Welcome@123 (not touched by tests). Test suite creates its own employee each run and changes password to NewPass@2026 for that ephemeral account.
seed_data_creation: Test suite creates a TEST_AuthEmp employee (phone +91 900000XXXX) per session and posts one TEST_ collection + one TEST_ expense. UI test creates a TEST_UI_<ts> employee and completes forced password change.
context_for_next_testing_agent: backend_test.py now uses Bearer-token auth end-to-end and exercises: login (admin+employee+invalid), me, change-password, role isolation, admin flows, identity-spoof prevention, logout. All 31 tests pass after the models.py fix. If you regenerate seed data, verify Collection/Expense responses still contain employee_id/employee_name. Playwright script must clear cookies (context.clear_cookies) — clearing localStorage alone is insufficient because login sets httpOnly access_token cookie.
rca of the issue: Collection(CollectionCreate) declared only id/receipt_number/created_at. Router code passed employee_id/employee_name as kwargs, but pydantic v2 defaults to 'ignore' for undeclared fields → both were dropped before insert. Consequence: every newly created record lost its owning employee, so (a) employee-scoped list_collections returned nothing for the creator, (b) admin activity aggregations were broken, (c) requirement #6 (server-side identity enforcement) failed by omission — there was no identity to enforce. Repro before fix: POST /api/collections as employee → 200 but response has no employee_id key; DB row also lacks it. Mitigation: added `employee_id: str` and `employee_name: str` fields to both Collection and Expense models. Post-fix retest: identity spoof attempts (payload sending employee_id='emp-raj', employee_name='SPOOF') return 200 with the signed-in employee's real id/name, and employee-scoped list endpoints return the new records.
